Anarthrous substantival adjective with the generic noun the ASV supplies to make it an English noun phrase (rule 46); headed on *great*, the word carrying the lexeme, by rule 31's subtraction test — *matters* alone is any matters.

Niphal participle used substantivally with the supplied generic *things* (rule 46), headed on *wonderful*; the unit is discontinuous around the *too* that belongs to the comparative preposition.

Comparative `מִן` rendered by the *too … for* frame; rule 24 gives both words to that one morpheme's discontinuous unit and heads it on the relational word *for*, since dropping *for* leaves the comparison with no relation stated. The competing reading leaves *too* with the participle, but rule 11 gives the function word first to the morpheme whose sense it carries.

review_notes: The ASV's marginal gloss *Hebrew walk* on *exercise myself* was read and set aside under rule 38; the printed text governs.
Both `וְ` + `לֹא` pairs are fused under rule 35 and headed on the negative; the two colons are read alike.

alignments.note: `אִם לֹא` rendered by the single *Surely*, which carries both morphemes' sense, so they share one unit under rule 30. Neither particle carries content the other lacks, so rule 23's syntactic-head direction puts the source head on the first morpheme; the competing reading heads on the negative.

The comparative phrase is the predicate of this verbless clause and `נַפְשִׁי` its subject, so the construction-supplied copula joins the preposition heading the predicate under rule 49; the unit is discontinuous around the substantive under rule 25. The competing reading puts *is* on the subject noun, but rule 20 sends the copula to the predicate wherever a predicate morpheme stands.

Article assimilated into the pointed preposition and supplied by MACULA as a token; the ASV writes *a weaned child* with no *the*, so it is unrepresented under rules 12 and 29. The indefinite *a* is the nominal expression's own under rule 15.
Substantival passive participle with its supplied generic noun and indefinite article, read exactly as the first occurrence and headed on *weaned*.
Preposition rendered *within*.

review_notes: The two `גָמֻל` phrases are aligned independently and identically; the article morpheme stands only in the second and is unrepresented there.
The copula of the final colon is placed on the comparative preposition under rule 49, the Hebrew clause making `נַפְשִׁי` the subject despite the ASV's English order.

alignments.note: Imperative rendered *hope*; the ASV writes no subject pronoun for it, the single supplied word standing before the vocative noun.

Preposition rendered *From*, opening the temporal range.

The adverb `עַתָּה` is rendered by the whole phrase *this time forth*; the supplied determiner and the particle belong to that one morpheme's rendering under rule 31, headed on *time*, the word carrying the lexeme. The competing head is *forth*, but dropping *time* leaves the phrase saying nothing.
Waw rendered *and* under rule 14.
`עַד` takes the *for* the ASV writes for its own relation; the waw beside it already holds the connective written for it, so no correlative pair is in question under rule 26.
Noun rendered *evermore*.

review_notes: The `מִן … עַד` range writes its second endpoint with a waw, so the waw takes the *and* and `עַד` takes the *for* written for its own relation (rule 26).
No source token is unrepresented in this verse and no target token is `added`.
